name: Jimmy Carter
role: 39th President of the United States (1977–1981); governor of Georgia; Nobel Peace laureate (2002)
summary: A Georgia Democrat and born-again Baptist who governed as a fiscally cautious centrist: he deregulated airlines and trucking and aimed at balanced budgets while backing energy conservation, environmental protection, affirmative action and the Equal Rights Amendment. His foreign policy centered on human rights, arms control and negotiated peace (Camp David, Panama treaties, SALT II), with a hardening after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan. After office he opposed the death penalty and the Iraq War, supported women's equality in religion, criticized money in politics and Israeli policy in the West Bank.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Listed adequate medical care for all Americans among the goals of his farewell address, promised first steps toward a national health plan in 1979, and in 2017 predicted the US would eventually adopt single-payer; no single universal scheme enacted.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed record: deregulated airlines, trucking, rail and beer and stressed private business as the main source of jobs, but also pursued energy planning, a windfall profits tax and the Chrysler loan guarantee.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Called the 1976 tax structure a disgrace and a welfare program for the rich and sought tax reform; in 2005 criticized tax changes that shifted burdens from the rich to working families.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed: deregulated economic sectors while defending health, safety and environmental regulation (OSHA, clean air and water) against Reagan in 1980 and backing better antitrust enforcement.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No stated position on legalising recreational drugs; his 1977 call to decriminalise cannabis possession is something nearby.

state-harmful.rationale: Said government has as its purpose to promote the well-being of its citizens, while acknowledging its limits.

limit-guns.rationale: Supported a ban on assault weapons and background checks for gun buyers (1994 letter with Ford and Reagan; later statements).

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said he supported same-sex marriage in civil ceremonies and that Jesus would approve; in 2014 said it should be left to the states.

abortion-legal.rationale: Personally opposed to abortion but accepted legal abortion after Roe v. Wade; in 2012 said he wished the Democratic Party would allow it only in cases of rape, incest or risk to the mother.

more-religion-public.rationale: In Our Endangered Values criticized the breakdown of the separation of church and state and religious fundamentalism in Washington.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His administration filed a brief supporting affirmative action in the Bakke case, appointed many minority and women judges and said minorities had been excluded from government.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called the UN the best avenue for peace and said Security Council decisions must be enforced.

free-trade.rationale: Promoted free trade with allies and said it must also be fair trade; highlighted multilateral trade negotiations.

nation-first.rationale: Said global challenges must be met with strong alliances and international consensus; promoted North-South cooperation.

limit-growth.rationale: Said healthy economic growth must continue and that energy conservation would help maintain living standards and jobs.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Listed constraints on global warming among the international agreements the world needs; did not describe drastic action.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 1976 said atomic power should be a last resort only, while not cutting it out; in 1980 criticized Reagan for emphasizing nuclear plants and urged stricter safety.

experts-over-public.rationale: Said every serious foreign policy mistake came from excluding the American people and promised to tap their common sense.

basic-income.rationale: In 1976 he said he would not favor a fixed income for people unless they cannot work.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Urged Congress to resist self-defeating protectionism, while protecting industry against unfair or illegal trade practices.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defended democratic government and criticized totalitarian states.

democracy-best.rationale: Said democratic methods are the most effective and that democracy works, and called human rights and democracy the basis of American policy.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said war is always an evil, never a good, even when necessary.

separate-church-state.rationale: Said the separation of church and state, a principle since Jefferson, has broken down and called that a moral crisis.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Defended separation of church and state against fundamentalist politics.

military-superiority.rationale: Pledged the US would remain the strongest of all nations and never neglect military strength, while seeking parity and reciprocal arms limits with the Soviet Union.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said no common mystique of blood or soil unites Americans, who are the most diverse nation, held together by a belief in human freedom.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Criticized the worship of self-indulgence and of special interests, saying the common good must prevail.

limit-population.rationale: Named overpopulation among resource problems that must be tackled with courage and foresight.

conscription.rationale: In 1980 ordered Selective Service registration and said the nation must be prepared for a draft, while hoping volunteer forces would suffice.

total-state.rationale: Defended protection of the individual from the arbitrary power of the state and criticized totalitarian states.

single-common-good.rationale: Warned that the national interest is not the sum of special interests and that the common good is our common interest and individual responsibility.

school-vouchers.rationale: No stated position on vouchers; opposing tuition tax credits for private schools is something nearby.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Said deficit spending should not be a feature of the budget in a time of high employment, cut the deficit and pledged to balance the budget; his stimulus was small and he put inflation first.

national-self-determination.rationale: Called collective security and self-determination profoundly important concepts embedded in international law.

force-without-un.rationale: Carter Doctrine and the 1980 hostage rescue attempt were unilateral, yet the Nobel lecture insisted Security Council decisions be enforced and he later opposed the Iraq War.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Faith was central to his public life and writing; stressed moral and spiritual values alongside reason.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare reform plan aimed at jobs so that those on welfare who are able to work can work; opposed income payments to people able to work.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Supported the Equal Rights Amendment and extension of its ratification period.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Cited opposition to racism and support for majority rule in Africa as foreign policy commitments and called for an end to discrimination.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Called for a shift to plentiful coal and a massive commitment to coal, shale and other domestic fuels so new demand is met from domestic production; also stressed conservation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Praised immigrants preserving their ethnic commitments, family structures and religion while forming a coherent society.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said discrimination and violence against women are pervasive worldwide, and that in the US women are paid less than men for the same work.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said Washington had become isolated and that special interests distort politics; ran in 1976 as an outsider.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Pursued health, welfare, education and energy programs; said government cannot solve everything but has a role in promoting well-being.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said the struggle for human rights overrides differences of color, nation or language and called for an end to discrimination against minorities and women.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said a president cannot lead without the support and consent of the people expressed through Congress.

separated-powers.rationale: Described the presidency as constrained by law, custom and the consent of Congress and said this is as it should be.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Called the growing chasm between rich and poor the greatest challenge and criticized policies favoring the rich at the expense of poor and working families; said inflation hits the poor hardest.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said immigrant groups preserving their ethnic and religious ties still form a coherent society that gives the nation its strength.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Warned against abandoning time-honored principles during hard times, calling American values necessities.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said thoughtful criticism and close scrutiny of officials by the press and public are an important part of democratic society.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Strengthened NATO ties and defense cooperation with allies.

death-penalty.rationale: Strong opponent of the death penalty; urged its prohibition in his Nobel lecture, sought abolition in New Mexico and backed clemency for death-row prisoners.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rejected the arguments of rulers who deny human rights to their people and made human rights a pillar of foreign policy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Said the industrialized world has not yet committed to share an appreciable part of its excessive wealth with the poor and called the rich-poor chasm the greatest problem.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Brokered Camp David with Israeli withdrawal from Sinai for peace; later said the premise had been that land would be swapped for peace under UN 242.

collective-defense.rationale: Reinforced and modernized NATO defense and proclaimed the Carter Doctrine defending Gulf allies.

ban-cartels.rationale: Called for better enforcement of antitrust laws and fewer government obstacles to competition to fight inflation.

no-bailouts.rationale: Secured the 1979 Chrysler Corporation Loan Guarantee Act, a federal loan guarantee for the failing automaker.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Supported affirmative action, though opposed racial quotas in college admissions.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Said too many Americans worship self-indulgence and consumption and that piling up material goods cannot fill the emptiness of lives without meaning.

corporate-influence.rationale: Described the US as having a system of unlimited political bribery after Citizens United and opposed that ruling.

job-guarantee.rationale: Listed a job for all those able to work as a goal and backed public service jobs and the Humphrey-Hawkins act, but the final act dropped the provision for a government employer of last resort.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: backed UN resolutions, international criminal courts and treaties as binding standards.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rejected an inordinate fear of communism and championed detente and arms control, while also confronting Soviet aggression in Afghanistan.

religion-illusion.rationale: Devout Christian who describes worshipping Jesus and treats religious faith as a source of meaning.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: he opposed the Briggs initiative against gay teachers, was the first president to meet gay rights activists and later backed civil same-sex marriage.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Made the release of political prisoners and the freedom of dissidents a central foreign policy aim.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said the US can never neglect its military strength and must remain strong.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Reinforced the bonds among democracies and NATO.

racial-franchise.rationale: Supported majority rule in Africa and opposed racism.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Named the threat of nuclear destruction first among three issues in his farewell and called preventing nuclear war the foremost responsibility.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Left the Southern Baptist Convention in 2000 over its bar on women pastors, saying women should play an absolutely equal role in service of Christ.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Left the Southern Baptist Convention after it adopted the view that wives should submit to husbands, objecting to the subservience of women.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Said war may sometimes be a necessary evil, which does not rule out lethal force to defend others; not a pacifist on this point.

person-over-state.rationale: Stressed protection of the individual from the arbitrary power of the state and the value and importance of the individual.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Described a moral and spiritual crisis and said owning things does not satisfy the longing for meaning.

future-generations.rationale: Warned that without action the world of 2000 would be less able to sustain life and urged stewardship of air, water and land.

arms-reduction.rationale: Sought substantial mutual reductions and eventual elimination of nuclear weapons, negotiated SALT II and called the arms race morally deplorable.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Said policy must be open and candid and should last longer than secret deals, and that excluding the public from foreign policy had led to mistakes.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Proposed tax incentives for low-income groups to lift incomes above poverty without making welfare more profitable than work.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Sought mutual, verified reductions while saying the US must remain strong, not unilateral disarmament.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Said religious traditions are a major cause of discrimination against women through false interpretations of scripture, while stressing that Jesus exalted women.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Called for an international criminal court to deter and punish war crimes and genocide.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Left the Southern Baptist Convention over a doctrinal statement favoring literal interpretation and rigidity, though he remained a devout Christian.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Opposed torture and persecution and defended individual protection against arbitrary state power; criticized torture at Guantanamo.

notes: Died December 2024. Abortion evidence is mixed (accepted legal abortion after Roe, personal opposition, 2012 wish for narrower Democratic stance), recorded at 0. Same-sex marriage: supported in civil ceremonies, in 2014 said states should decide. His full texts of the 1977 inaugural address, Our Endangered Values, Palestine: Peace Not Apartheid and A Call to Action were not reachable; the books are known here only through his interviews. Several high-confidence answers rest on speeches from different years; the most recent clear position was used. His 2015 'oligarchy' remark was not opened; the Citizens United 'unlimited political bribery' quote was used instead.
